newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Pol Pot trial a decision for Cambodians.
newsitem.headline: China says Pol Pot trial a decision for Cambodians.

text.p: China on Tuesday hinted its opposition to a plan by the United States to try Khmer Rouge guerrilla chief Pol Pot by an international tribunal for crimes against humanity.

"We believe... the question of Pol Pot is Cambodia's internal affair," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai said when asked to comment on China's stand on an international tribunal for the infamous leader.
"It should be decided by Cambodians themselves without foreign interference," Cui said.

The United States has asked Canada to help to extradite Pol Pot from Cambodia so he can be tried by an international tribunal for the deaths of more than one million people during his brutal 1975-79 "killing fields" regime.
U.S. officials have said the issue was complicated and they did not have a final answer from Canada.
Pol Pot fled the northwest Khmer Rouge base of Anlong Veng earlier this month after the execution of his defence chief and almost a dozen of his family members.
Cambodian government leaders have announced Pol Pot was captured by his former Khmer Rouge allies last Thursday, but the United States is awaiting confirmation that he is in custody.
The Cambodian government has been adamant that Pol Pot be taken out of the country for fear of mob violence and the political repercussions of his arrest.
